title: How to organize the linen shelf zone | Hall Closet
description:
Holds the sheets, towels, and blankets the beds in this house actually rotate through.

This is the Linen Shelf Zone in the Hall Closet. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Three sheet sets per bed, each nested inside one of its own pillowcases, with the bed size written on the shelf edge underneath. Everyday towels folded to one width in a stack no taller than your forearm. Two spare blankets on the top shelf with nothing balanced on them.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Unfold every set and check it is complete and fits a bed you still own.
Straighten: Fold each set to one uniform footprint and bundle it inside its own pillowcase so a bed change is one grab, no
Shine: Pull every stack right out, wipe the shelf boards with a barely damp cloth, and let the wood dry fully before
Safety: A tall stack on a high shelf comes down as one mass when you tug the bottom towel.
Standardize: The shelf label carries the count, not just the name: "Queen, 3 sets." Anyone opening this door can see the sh
Sustain: Stripping a bed sends you here for the fresh bundle, and the count on the label tells you on the spot whether

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Three sets per bed, each nested in its own pillowcase, with the size and count written on the shelf edge.
